calls.head: Shots should fly both ways
calls.body: Nashville plays some of the league’s fastest games, and so does Toronto. We think this one runs hotter than either team’s usual.
calls.call: The game runs at more than 84.4 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, faster than either team’s usual.
calls.nums: Pace (shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams): Nashville 4th (84.4), Toronto 5th (84.4)
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: The game ran at 81.8 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined, against the faster team’s usual 84.4 and a league average of 82.0.

calls.head: The Predators kill penalties far better than the Maple Leafs
calls.body: The Predators are around the middle of the league for the penalty kill, at the airtight end; the Maple Leafs are one of the league’s worst, at the leaky end. Expect that gap to show.
calls.call: The Predators’ penalty kill allows less per 60 than the Maple Leafs’.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: On expected goals allowed per 60 on the penalty kill, Nashville had 12.3 per 60 and Toronto 34.3 per 60. Coming in, Nashville was at 7.5 per 60 and Toronto at 8.4 per 60.

TOR.head: We had this close to even (44% for Toronto), and Toronto came through.

NSH.head: We had this close to even (56% for Nashville), and it went Toronto’s way.

surprises.head: Nashville got the good looks
surprises.body: Nashville’s shots at 5-on-5 were more dangerous than usual: a 9.1% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 5.9% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 60 games.

surprises.head: Nashville shortened their bench
surprises.body: Nashville’s bottom-six forwards played 38% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 42% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 9 games.

story.head: The Maple Leafs come back from three down
paras: Steven Stamkos opened the scoring midway through the first. Five different Maple Leafs scored. The Predators led by three, but the Maple Leafs came all the way back. Auston Matthews won it in overtime.
The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way.

items.text: One of the preview’s two calls held.
